concerns.text: The plan relies exclusively on GTEx v8 RNA‑seq TPM matrices and phenotype files to assess Metabolic Syndrome (MetS) status. GTEx donors are predominantly healthy post‑mortem samples and lack a sufficient number of true MetS cases; many donors are missing required clinical variables, leading to extensive exclusions. Consequently, GTEx is an inappropriate primary dataset for investigating a correlation between circadian gene expression and MetS risk. A dataset with clinically ascertained MetS diagnoses (e.g., a cohort study like MESA, UK Biobank, or a disease‑focused biobank) should be used or GTEx should be supplemented with such a resource to ensure adequate case numbers and phenotype validity.
